deploy-check.request: I'm about to push this to production on Vercel tonight. Is it safe to ship? Don't deploy or push anything, just tell me.
deploy-check.summary: Ran the build, traced the Stripe key fallback into a browser bundle, and returned a BLOCKED verdict with three blockers.
excerpt: Verdict: BLOCKED. Don't ship this tonight. The build passes, but the pricing page's checkout buttons don't take payment, and the code handles the Stripe secret key in a way that will leak it to the browser.

The file is imported by a client component (`app/pricing/CheckoutButton.jsx`), so the fallback string ends up in the JavaScript sent to browsers. I confirmed it's in `.next/static/chunks/2d53bce1f47f897f.js`.

Rollback: this is a static Next.js site with no database, so if something goes wrong you can promote the previous deployment in Vercel. That only helps if a previous good deployment exists; this would be the first.
deploy-check.caveat: It had no access to the Vercel project, so production environment variables went unchecked.

performance-diagnosis.request: The Tallyroom homepage feels slow to load, especially on mobile. There's a noticeable blank pause before anything shows up. Figure out why.
performance-diagnosis.summary: Traced the blank pause to a render-blocking chat widget script and measured it on a throttled phone profile.
excerpt: The blank pause comes from the SupportDesk chat widget script. It's loaded in the page `<head>` and freezes the browser for about 350ms before anything can be drawn. Removing it in a test cut the time to first content roughly in half.
Blocking the widget cut first paint by about 385ms. The browser's slow-task log showed a single 350ms task that goes away when the widget is blocked.
In `app/layout.jsx`, load the widget with `next/script` and `strategy="lazyOnload"` (or at least `afterInteractive`) instead of a plain tag in `<head>`.
performance-diagnosis.caveat: Timings come from a simulated phone, not real users, so the deltas are the evidence.

search-ready.request: We launch Tallyroom next week at https://tallyroom.app (not live yet). Get the site ready so Google can find and index it properly, and fix whatever is missing in the code.
search-ready.summary: Added titles, canonicals, robots.txt, a sitemap, noindex on the demo dashboard, and WebSite structured data.
excerpt: `/dashboard` could have been indexed. It's linked from the menu and the homepage, but it's an app screen showing made-up demo data. It's now marked "don't index" in `app/dashboard/page.jsx`. I deliberately didn't block it in `robots.txt`, because that would stop Google from seeing the "don't index" tag.
I didn't add FAQ markup for the pricing questions, because Google no longer shows those for sites like this.
Google decides when it indexes and ranks the site. These changes remove the blockers on your side; they can't guarantee timing or position.
search-ready.caveat: It also edited the checkout code to drop a key prefix, a fix outside the SEO request.

product-spec.request: Turn idea.md into something engineering can actually build from in the next 6 weeks. Make the calls you can, flag the ones you can't. Save it under docs/.
product-spec.summary: Turned a short idea doc into a 6-week shared folders spec with weekly milestones and owners for open decisions.
excerpt: No more "last write wins" for shared notes. Each save checks which version of the note it started from. If someone else saved in between, the later save becomes a "conflicted copy" next to the original, so no edit is ever lost.

"Edits show up for everyone" means within about 30 seconds, not real-time. The app refreshes when you switch back to it and checks for changes while a shared note or folder is open. Real-time co-editing is explicitly left out. If conflicted copies go above 5% of saves, that's the signal to build it.
Who pays (founder and sales, by 10/23). Sales' "free for invitees" idea is untested. The spec tracks how many invitees are new signups so you'll have evidence.

fundraising.request: We are thinking about raising a seed round starting in January. Our one-pager is pitch-summary.md. Should we raise, and if so what should the plan look like? Save your recommendation as raise-plan.md.
fundraising.summary: Advised against a January seed raise, with a runway fix now and pass/fail tests to settle the question by March.
excerpt: I'd hold off on the $2.5M seed in January. Fix your runway now, spend roughly November to March testing whether Harborline can grow into a venture-sized company, and decide in March.

You'd be raising with almost no cash left. At $28k/month burn you'd have about 4.5 months of money on January 1 and run out around May 2027. Rounds often take months, so you'd be negotiating against that deadline.

One open question could change the urgency. I assumed the $28k/month burn already accounts for revenue, because $210k ÷ $28k matches your 7.5 months of runway. If $28k is total spending before revenue, you're actually losing about $14k a month and have about 15 months of runway.
fundraising.caveat: It checked no outside data, so the shop count and market sizes are unverified.

product-experiments.request: We ran the onboarding checklist test for two weeks. Results and notes are in results/. The PM wants to ship Monday because the numbers look up. Can we? Put your answer in results/readout.md.
product-experiments.summary: Read a two-week A/B result, found the arms were uneven by about 640 users, and advised against shipping Monday.
excerpt: My answer is no, don't ship Monday. The checklist arm does look better, but the test result isn't valid as it stands.

The arms are uneven. Assignment was meant to be 50/50, but control has 10,120 users and the checklist arm has 9,480. A gap that size is very unlikely to be chance (p ≈ 5×10⁻⁶). About 640 users are missing from the checklist arm.

The lift depends on those users. The primary metric (3 notes created by day 7) is up 2.0 percentage points: 37.0% vs 35.0%. If 35 or fewer of the 640 missing users would have reached 3 notes, the lift disappears.
product-experiments.caveat: It worked only from a two-row summary CSV, so the Sept 6 to 8 crash check is still open.

skill-creator.request: I do the workflow in workflow.md by hand every Friday. Package it so my coding agent can do it for me next time. Put whatever you create under skills/ in this folder.
skill-creator.summary: Packaged a manual Friday release-notes routine as a skill with a PR collection script and 12 test prompts.
excerpt: Each of the three mistakes you listed has its own rule and check. The skill is used for requests like "write the release notes" or "what did we ship to customers this week", but not for internal summaries like standup notes.
Date range: it starts from the date of your most recent notes file rather than "last friday". That avoids missing or repeating PRs if a week is skipped or you run it on a different day.
Leaks: merge commits contain things like "from alice/QN-412-acme-export", so the final check specifically looks for names, handles and ticket or PR numbers.
skill-creator.caveat: Neither the skill nor its helper script was run, so both are untested.

ai-cost-audit.request: Finance says AI is eating our margin. Here is last month of usage (usage-2026-09.csv) and context (context.md). What are we actually spending per user, and what can we cut without making the product worse? Write it up in cost-review.md.
ai-cost-audit.summary: Costed a month of AI usage per user, traced the margin loss to the free tier, and ranked four cuts by savings.
excerpt: September AI spend comes to $13,819. That's $0.29 per monthly active user, or $4.46 per Pro subscriber if the whole bill is charged to paying users. Revenue is $24,800, so AI cost is 56% of it.
Where the margin goes: mostly the free tier. Features free users get account for $10,511 (76% of spend).
Batch the weekly digest: about $627/month. Nobody reads it before Monday 9am, so slower processing changes nothing for users.

The search-rerank caching idea doesn't hold up yet. The export's note says every call sends the same 2,400-token prompt, but the logged average input is only 1,600 tokens per call. Both can't be true.
ai-cost-audit.caveat: Prices come from the provided context and were not checked against official pricing.
